reason: The text establishes that Yahweh is the foundational God of the Hebrew people through multiple emphases: (1) He identifies Himself as 'the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob,' directly linking Yahweh to the patriarchal covenant tradition; (2) He explicitly frames the Hebrews as 'my people' (עַמִּי), establishing a covenantal relationship; (3) The purpose of their liberation is framed as enabling them to serve God: 'you shall serve God on this mountain' (תַּֽעַבְדוּן אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים); (4) Yahweh's name (יְהוָה - YHWH) is revealed as the eternal identifier for this relationship. The narrative structure presents the Hebrews' primary identity and raison d'être as bound to their relationship with Yahweh.
